supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for NWD\leo.martins from 203.0.113.250, using NTLM; both report an incorrect-password substatus.
The domain controller recorded a successful network logon for NWD\leo.martins from the same IP about one minute after the second failure; this logon used Kerberos.
The failures followed by a successful logon from the same recorded source warrant investigation, but the records alone do not establish that the logons were unauthorized or malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The authentication records show the source address and authentication results, but do not identify the device or person using that address.
The available records do not show what resources were accessed after the successful logon or whether the session was used for any actions.
No corroborating network, endpoint, or account-activity telemetry for the logon is included.
claims_not_established: Whether 203.0.113.250 corresponds to an authorized or unauthorized source in this environment.
Whether the successful Kerberos logon was made by leo.martins or by someone else using the account.
Whether the successful logon was related to the preceding failed attempts.
Whether any access or changes occurred as a result of the successful logon.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm the source address against network, firewall, DHCP, and other available connection records for the relevant time.
Review domain-controller authentication details and any related account or resource access events around 13:40–14:20 UTC.
Review WS-LMARTINS-01 and any identified source device for session, credential-use, and process activity around the logons.
Confirm with the account owner and IT whether the successful logon and its source were expected.
